mainTopic: קמיצה and קידוש in a כלי on the ground, whether blood and the קומץ become holy when split between two כלים, and leftover blood on the כהן's finger.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב ששת's proof that a כהן may take the קמיצה from a כלי resting on the ground. The proof is that the לחם הפנים משנה counts every כהן, yet never mentions anyone lifting the שלחן before the בזיכין are removed. רבא says this is obvious, and adds that a מנחה may also be sanctified in a כלי on the ground. He then asks whether קידוש קומץ follows the rules of a מנחה or of blood, and decides it follows blood. That forces him to take back his earlier ruling that a קומץ split between two כלים becomes holy. The גמרא looks for the source that split blood is not holy. It finds it in the sprinkling-water rule, the words 'וטבל' and 'בדם', and a ברייתא about the פר כהן משיח. From the words 'מן הדם', רבא learns that leftover blood on the finger is פסול, and he defends this against challenges from a ברייתא and from the פרה אדומה משנה. The amud ends by asking whether רבי אלעזר really holds that split blood is not holy, since he says the חביתי כהן גדול becomes holy in halves; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה never mentions lifting the Table
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's proof ends with the point that the לחם הפנים משנה never says a כהן lifts the שלחן before the בזיכין are removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet the משנה does not teach that someone lifts the Table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started before this section. The משנה describes the whole changing of the לחם הפנים but never says anyone lifts the שלחן off the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בזיכין sit on the שלחן, which stands on the floor of the היכל. If they are removed without lifting the Table, then taking something out of a כלי resting on the ground is fine. רב ששת wants to apply this to the קמיצה of a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: lifts up
the Table in the היכל that holds the לחם הפנים
it does not teach (it is not mentioned in the משנה)

phrases.english: and yet, 'he lifts the Table'
is not taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ מַגְבִּיהַּ אֶת הַשּׁוּלְחָן לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's proof begun before this section.
steps.raayaObject: קמיצה may be done from a כלי resting on the ground.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of לחם הפנים (מנחות 99b), which leaves out any lifting of the שלחן when the בזיכין are removed.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה only lists the order of the services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה may only be listing the main steps of the service, not every physical detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't you say there that the תנא was only listing the order of the services? Here too, he is only listing the order of the services.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to knock down רב ששת's proof. It argues that leaving something out of the משנה proves nothing, because the משנה is not giving every detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere (on 12a) we explained a missing detail by saying the תנא only gives the order of the עבודות. If the same applies here, lifting the שלחן could still be required even though it is not mentioned. That would make the silence of the משנה meaningless as a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: the order of the Temple services
he (the תנא) mentioned or cited
there (in a different משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not deny the rule. It only says this particular proof is weak, because the משנה might be skipping details.

phrases.english: Didn't you say there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה on 12a about wrong intentions during the מנחה service.

phrases.english: that he cited the order of the services?
Here too, he cited the order of the services.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמְרַתְּ הָתָם, סֵדֶר עֲבוֹדוֹת נָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה's silence, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא may list only the main steps, so a missing detail like lifting the Table proves nothing.

steps.title: The two משניות are not alike, since this one counts the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the pushback. The לחם הפנים משנה counts how many כהנים take part, so a כהן lifting the Table would have been listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they the same? There, the תנא did not go into the number of כהנים. Here, he does go into the number of כהנים. If it were so, let him teach that someone lifts the Table!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback and brings the proof back. It shows that this משנה is far more detailed than the one on 12a.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 12a משנה only gives the general order, so leaving things out is normal there. Our משנה counts each כהן and what he holds. If lifting the Table were needed, it would need another כהן, and the משנה would have counted him.

keyTerms.meaning: are they comparable? (a way of rejecting a comparison)
goes into the count (gives exact numbers)
if it were so
let him teach it

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There, he did not go into the number of priests;
here, he does go into the number of priests.
If it were so, let him teach 'he lifts'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם לָא נָחֵית לְמִנְיָינָא דְּכֹהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the דחיה of step 2 and brings back the proof of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison in step 2 between the 12a משנה and the לחם הפנים משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה that counts the כהנים is giving full detail, so leaving out a lifting כהן is meaningful.

steps.title: Conclusion: קמיצה may be done from a כלי on the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the משנה that קמיצה may be done from a כלי resting on the ground, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from it: we may take the קמיצה from a כלי that is resting on the ground. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion of רב ששת's proof and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the בזיכין are removed from a Table standing on the floor, removing something from a כלי on the ground is acceptable in the עבודה. The same applies to the קמיצה of a מנחה, so the כהן does not need to hold the כלי up.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it (a proof is accepted)
we take a handful (קמיצה) of the מנחה
a vessel resting on the ground

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha here: a כהן may do קמיצה from a כלי that is sitting on the ground. This is proven from the removal of the בזיכין from the שלחן.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
we may take a handful from a vessel resting on the ground.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: קוֹמְצִין מִכְּלִי שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion once the pushback has been rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קמיצה from a כלי resting on the ground is valid.

steps.title: רבא: both קמיצה and קידוש may be done in a כלי on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is obvious that קמיצה may be done from a כלי on the ground, based on removing the בזיכין. He adds that a מנחה may be sanctified in a כלי on the ground, based on setting the בזיכין down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me that one may take the handful from a כלי on the ground, since we find this when the בזיכין are removed. One may also sanctify a מנחה in a כלי on the ground, since we find this when the בזיכין are set in place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives two rules and says both are obvious to him. Each rule is copied from a matching step in the לחם הפנים service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the בזיכין from the Table on the floor matches קמיצה, which takes something out of a כלי. Placing the בזיכין on the Table on the floor matches קידוש, which puts the מנחה into a כלי שרת. So taking out and putting in are both fine while the כלי is on the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious to me
for we find (a model case)
removing the bowls of frankincense
we sanctify a מנחה by placing it in a כלי שרת
arranging (setting down) the bowls of frankincense

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both steps of the מנחה, putting it into the כלי and taking the handful out, can be done with the כלי on the ground, each with its own model from the שלחן.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me
that one takes a handful from a vessel resting on the ground,
for we find this with the removal of the bowls.

phrases.aramaic: מְקַדְּשִׁין מִנְחָה בִּכְלִי שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע –
phrases.english: One may sanctify a meal offering in a vessel resting on the ground,
for we find this with the arranging of the bowls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with the conclusion of step 4 and adds a second rule about קידוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both קמיצה from, and קידוש in, a כלי resting on the ground are valid, modeled on removing and arranging the בזיכין.

steps.title: רבא asks which model the handful follows
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether קידוש קומץ is learned from a מנחה or from דם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: when we put the handful into a vessel to make it holy, what is the rule? Do we learn it from a meal offering, or do we learn it from blood?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question: does putting the קומץ into a כלי that rests on the ground work, like a מנחה, or not, like blood?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבא showed that a מנחה may be sanctified in a כלי on the ground. Blood, however, must be collected in a כלי that is not resting on the ground. The קומץ sits between these two, so רבא asks which one it resembles.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a real question (a dilemma)
Making the handful holy by putting it into a holy vessel
We learn it, we derive it
Meal offering

phrases.english: Rava asks:
Sanctifying the handful, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means putting the קומץ into a כלי that is resting on the ground, continuing from רבא's last statement.

phrases.english: Do we learn it from a meal offering,
or do we learn it from blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's rulings about the מנחה, he asks about the קומץ, which is not clearly like the מנחה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קידוש קומץ in a כלי on the ground follows the rules of a מנחה (allowed) or of blood (not allowed).

steps.title: רבא answers: learn it from blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא himself resolves that the קומץ is learned from blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then answered his own question: we learn it from blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question: the קומץ follows the rules of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since blood cannot be collected in a כלי resting on the ground, the same rule now applies to the קומץ. This also means other blood rules may carry over to the קומץ, and the next step builds its challenge on exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: He then resolved it himself
Blood of an offering

phrases.english: He then resolved it:
We learn it from blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קידוש קומץ is learned from blood, so it is not done in a כלי resting on the ground.

steps.title: Contradiction from רבא's ruling on a split handful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא elsewhere rules a קומץ split into two כלים is holy, which does not fit with learning from blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But it was taught: if a כהן split a handful between two vessels, רב נחמן says it is not holy, and רבא says it is holy. If the handful is learned from blood, then let him learn from blood that it is not holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. It points to another ruling of his that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that is split between two כלים does not become holy. If the קומץ follows blood, then a split קומץ should also not become holy. Yet רבא ruled that it is holy, so his two statements clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opening of a contradiction)
That he divided into two vessels
It is sanctified, holy
And if it is so

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבא is the one saying the split קומץ IS holy, and רב נחמן says it is not. Don't flip them.

phrases.english: And did Rava really say this?
But it was stated:
A handful that one divided into two vessels,
Rav Nachman says: it is not sanctified,
and Rava says: it is sanctified.
And if so, let him learn from blood!
phrases.notes: The idea is that blood split into two vessels is not holy, so the קומץ should be the same. The גמרא proves this about blood in a moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 7 using his own ruling elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that קידוש קומץ is learned from blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the קומץ follows blood, and split blood is not holy, then a split קומץ should not be holy. But רבא ruled that it is.

steps.title: רבא retracted his split-handful ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא took back his ruling about the split קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא retracted that ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction: רבא changed his mind about the split קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he decided the קומץ is learned from blood, רבא dropped his earlier view that a split קומץ is holy. Now he agrees that a split קומץ is not holy, just like split blood. His two statements no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted, changed his mind
From that (earlier) ruling

phrases.english: Rava retracted from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two conflicting statements was withdrawn.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבא held two conflicting positions.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא withdrew the split-קומץ ruling. He holds that the קומץ follows blood, so a split קומץ is not holy.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final view: the קומץ follows the rules of blood. It cannot be sanctified in a כלי on the ground, and it cannot be sanctified when split between two כלים.

steps.title: Source for blood not being sanctified in halves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that blood split into two כלים is not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding blood, from where do we know that it is not sanctified in halves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule about blood that the challenge in step 8 relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole challenge assumed that split blood is not holy. Now the גמרא asks where that assumption comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
In halves, in parts

phrases.english: And blood, from where do we know
that it is not sanctified in halves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the blood rule that steps 8 and 9 took for granted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that blood split between two כלים is not sanctified.

steps.title: רב תחליפא's teaching about split sprinkling water
steps.stepSummary: The source is רב תחליפא בן שאול's teaching: if less than a sprinkling amount was sanctified in each of two כלים, nothing became sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב תחליפא בן שאול taught: if he sanctified less than enough for sprinkling in this vessel, and less than enough for sprinkling in that vessel, he has not sanctified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching about sprinkling water. When the amount is split so that neither כלי has enough to sprinkle, it does not become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching shows that a split amount does not add up to one sanctified amount. The גמרא wants to apply the same idea to blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough for one sprinkling
Less than
He has not sanctified it

phrases.english: As Rav Tachlifa ben Shaul taught:

phrases.aramaic: קִידֵּשׁ פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי הַזָּאָה בִּכְלִי זֶה,
phrases.english: If he sanctified less than enough for sprinkling in this vessel,
phrases.notes: This is about the sprinkling water (מי חטאת), not blood. That's why the next step asks whether we can apply it to blood.

phrases.english: and less than enough for sprinkling in that vessel,
he has not sanctified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 with a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the case of sprinkling water: split amounts, each too small to sprinkle, are not sanctified.

steps.title: Can the sprinkling-water rule apply to blood?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask whether the sprinkling-water rule is a special הלכה, which would mean we cannot learn blood from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they asked: regarding blood, what is the law? Is the sprinkling-water rule a הלכה given to משה at סיני, and from such a הלכה we do not learn other cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own source. Maybe the sprinkling-water rule is a special הלכה, and then it cannot be applied to blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני is a rule handed down by tradition, and we do not use it to build other laws. If the sprinkling-water rule is that kind of הלכה, then the source for split blood falls away. The other side of the question comes next in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
A הלכה למשה מסיני, a rule known by tradition
We do not learn other cases from such a tradition

steps.whyThisMatters: If blood cannot be learned from the sprinkling water, then the rule that split blood is not holy needs a new source. That rule is the basis of the challenge to רבא in step 8.

phrases.english: And a question was raised:
With blood, what is the law?
Is it a tradition from Sinai,
phrases.notes: "It" means the sprinkling-water rule from רב תחליפא.

phrases.english: and from such a tradition we do not learn other cases?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the source in step 11 can be applied to blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the sprinkling-water rule is a הלכה למשה מסיני that cannot be extended to blood.

steps.title: The other side of the question: maybe the rule comes from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question. Maybe the rule for מי חטאת comes from the words 'וטבל במים', and blood has the same kind of wording, 'וטבל בדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the reason there, by the sprinkling water, is because the פסוק says 'and dip in the water.' If so, here too by blood, doesn't the פסוק say 'and dip in the blood'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question it opened in step 12. Maybe the rule is not a special הלכה at all, but comes from a פסוק that also appears by blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the worry was that the water rule is a one-time הלכה, so we cannot learn blood from it. Here the other option is raised: the water rule comes from the word 'וטבל', which means one must dip into a real amount. The same word is written by blood, so blood would follow the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. It opens the second side of a question.
And he shall dip. This means dipping into liquid that is really there.
The water of purification, mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: Or perhaps, there, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the sprinkling water from step 11.

phrases.english: Because it is written: "And dip in the water."
Here too, isn't it written: "And dip in the blood"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the two-sided question begun in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the water rule a special הלכה that cannot be applied to other cases, or does it come from 'וטבל', a word also written by blood?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר rules that split blood is also not holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא quotes רבי אלעזר: blood split into two כלים, with less than the full amount in each, does not become holy either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was said: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: even with blood, he did not make it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that answers the question. Blood follows the same rule as the sprinkling water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (even) shows that blood is treated just like מי חטאת. If the full amount was not collected in one כלי, the כלי does not make the blood holy. This fits the second side of the question, that the rule comes from 'וטבל'.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, also. Here it means blood is just like the water.
He did not sanctify. The כלי did not make it holy.

phrases.english: And it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Even with blood, he did not sanctify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 12 and 13 by ruling that blood follows the water rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Split blood, with less than the full amount in each כלי, is not made holy, the same as מי חטאת.

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא about the פר כהן משיח
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports רבי אלעזר with a ברייתא. 'וטבל' teaches that the כהן dips into real blood and does not wipe the walls of the כלי. 'בדם' teaches that a dipping amount must be there from the start. 'מן הדם' teaches that the blood must come from the blood of this matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a ברייתא also teaches this. About the bull of the anointed כהן, the פסוק says 'and he shall dip,' so he dips and does not wipe. It says 'in the blood,' so the blood must hold a dipping amount from the start. It says 'of the blood,' so he sprinkles from the blood of this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to prove that blood needs a full amount in the כלי from the start. This supports רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads each word of the פסוק as its own rule. 'וטבל' rules out wiping the last drops off the walls of the כלי. 'בדם' requires the right amount to be in the כלי from the beginning, which is the same idea as the split-כלים rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought as a חטאת by the anointed כהן גדול
Wiping. Getting the last drops off the walls of the כלי with the finger.
The amount of blood needed to dip a finger
From the start, from the beginning

phrases.english: Rava said: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא:
Regarding the bull of the anointed priest:
phrases.notes: The printed letters look odd, but they are read as פר כהן משיח, the bull of the anointed כהן.

phrases.english: "And he shall dip": he dips, and does not wipe.
"In the blood": there must be in the blood
a measure for dipping from the start.
"Of the blood": from the blood of the matter.
phrases.notes: He means the blood this section of the פסוק is talking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that blood must be collected in the full amount in one כלי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'וטבל' and 'בדם' by the פר כהן משיח as requiring a real dipping amount from the start
steps.whatToRemember: Blood of a חטאת, like מי חטאת, must be in the כלי in the full amount from the start. Splitting it between two כלים does not work.

steps.title: Why the תורה needed both 'וטבל' and 'בדם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both words are needed. From 'וטבל' alone, we might think enough blood for one dip is fine, even without enough for all seven sprinklings. So the תורה added 'בדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both 'and he shall dip' and 'in the blood' had to be written. If the תורה had written only 'and he shall dip,' I would have said it is fine even if he did not collect enough for all the dips, which is seven sprinklings from the start. So the תורה wrote 'in the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא deals with a quiet question: why does the תורה need two words that seem to teach the same thing? It explains what the second word adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וטבל' alone would only require enough blood for a single dip. 'בדם' teaches that from the start there must be enough for all the dippings, meaning seven sprinklings. So each word teaches its own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary. It shows that a word in the פסוק is not extra.
I would have thought. This is the mistaken first idea.
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Sprinkling seven times, as done with the bull's blood

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two amounts. 'וטבל' alone would only require enough for one dip. 'בדם' requires enough for all seven sprinklings from the start.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "and he shall dip,"
and it was necessary to write "in the blood,"
because if the Merciful One had written only "and he shall dip,"
I would have said:
even though he did not collect
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the end of the thought: it would still be fine, as long as there is enough for one dip.

phrases.english: a measure for all the dippings,
that is, enough to sprinkle seven times from the start,
so the Merciful One wrote "in the blood."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the two words in the ברייתא of step 15 are not repeating each other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word in the פסוק teaches a separate rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From 'וטבל' alone, enough blood for one dip would be fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בדם' requires enough blood for all seven sprinklings to be in the כלי from the start.

steps.title: Why 'בדם' alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written only 'בדם', we might think the כהן may even wipe the walls of the כלי. So the תורה also wrote 'וטבל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'in the blood', I would have said that even wiping the blood off the walls is fine. So the תורה wrote 'and he shall dip'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 16. It shows the other direction: why 'וטבל' is still needed even though we have 'בדם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בדם' only tells us a full dipping amount must be there at the start. Without 'וטבל', we might think that once there was enough at the start, the כהן may wipe up the last drops from the walls. 'וטבל' teaches that he must really dip into blood each time.

keyTerms.meaning: Wiping, scraping up blood from the walls of the כלי instead of dipping into it
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Both words are needed. 'בדם' requires a full dipping amount from the start. 'וטבל' requires a real dip every time, with no wiping of the walls.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'in the blood',
I would have said: even if he wipes,
phrases.notes: He means: if there was enough blood at the start, he could wipe up what is left from the walls.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote 'and he shall dip'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'both words are needed' answer begun in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא (each word is needed for its own lesson)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'בדם', wiping the walls would be allowed as long as there was enough blood at the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וטבל' rules out wiping; a real dip is needed each time.

steps.title: What does 'מן הדם' come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the last part of the ברייתא and asks what 'from the blood of this matter' comes to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From the blood of this matter': what does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the third phrase of the ברייתא from step 15. It asks what case these words are meant to rule out, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word in the פסוק should teach something. 'מן הדם' seems extra, so the גמרא asks which kind of blood it makes unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave a case out of the rule
Of this matter, meaning the blood that belongs to this specific service

phrases.english: 'From the blood of this matter':
what does it come to exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first two words of the ברייתא to its third phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case 'מן הדם' comes to rule out.

steps.title: רבא: it excludes blood left on the finger
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'מן הדם' excludes the blood left on the כהן's finger from the previous sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it excludes the leftover blood on the finger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The כהן may not sprinkle again with blood still left on his finger; he must dip again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After each sprinkling some blood stays on the finger. 'מן הדם' means each sprinkling must come straight from the blood in the כלי, not from those leftover drops.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover blood on the finger after a sprinkling

phrases.english: Rava said: to exclude the leftovers on the finger,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מן הדם' excludes sprinkling with blood left on the finger from the last sprinkling.

steps.title: This supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא's reading backs up רבי אלעזר, who says leftover blood on the finger is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אלעזר, who said: the leftover blood on the finger is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא, as רבא reads it, agrees with a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר already said שירים שבאצבע are פסולין. Now a ברייתא teaches the same thing from 'מן הדם', so his view has a source. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him, it backs up his view
Unfit, not valid for the service

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Elazar,
who said: the leftovers on the finger are unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבא's answer supports an earlier ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that שירים שבאצבע are פסולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'מן הדם שבענין' as explained by רבא.

steps.title: A ברייתא about blood that sprayed onto a garment
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא quotes a ברייתא: if blood sprayed from the כהן's hand before he sprinkled, the garment must be washed. If it sprayed after he sprinkled, it need not be washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said to רבא: Your students say in the name of רב עמרם that a ברייתא teaches: If a כהן was sprinkling and some blood sprayed from his hand, then if it was before he sprinkled, the garment must be washed. If it was after he sprinkled, it need not be washed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין בר רב אדא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבא. This step only lays out the ברייתא; the problem it causes is explained in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of a חטאת that is fit for sprinkling makes a garment need washing (כיבוס). So the ברייתא tells us when the blood on the כהן's hand still counts as fit blood. Before he sprinkled, it is fit; after he sprinkled, it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling (the כהן doing the sprinkling)
It sprayed, it splashed off
A sprinkling, here the blood meant for sprinkling
Needs washing (the garment must be laundered)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said to Rava:
Your students say that Rav Amram said,
it was taught in a ברייתא: if he was sprinkling
and the sprinkling blood sprayed from his hand,
phrases.notes: It sprayed onto a garment. Blood of a חטאת on a garment means the garment must be washed (ויקרא 6:20).

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִזָּה – טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס,
phrases.english: if it was before he sprinkled, the garment needs washing;
if after he sprinkled, it does not need washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that will be used against רבא and רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading and רבי אלעזר's ruling that שירים שבאצבע are פסולין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא ties the need for washing to whether the sprinkling was done yet. The next step uses that to argue that leftover blood is still fit.

steps.title: So leftover blood on the finger is כשר
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא reads the ברייתא as 'before he finished all his sprinklings'. That would mean the leftover blood on the finger between sprinklings is still fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it mean before he finished his sprinkling, and after he finished his sprinkling? Learn from this that the leftover blood on the finger is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין בר רב אדא explains why the ברייתא is a problem for רבא. If 'before he sprinkled' means before all the sprinklings were done, then leftover blood in the middle still makes a garment need washing, so it must be fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only fit blood makes a garment need washing. If blood spraying off between sprinklings still requires washing, that leftover blood must be fit for sprinkling. This goes against רבי אלעזר, who said it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean...? (suggesting a reading of a source)
Finished his sprinkling, completed all the sprinklings
Learn from this, so we can conclude
Fit, valid for the service

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge depends on reading 'before he sprinkled' as 'before he finished ALL the sprinklings'. If it means only before one single sprinkling, the proof would not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a direct clash with רבי אלעזר and רבא about whether a כהן must dip again before every sprinkling.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָּמַר הַזָּאָתוֹ,
phrases.english: Doesn't it mean: before he finished his sprinkling,
and after he finished his sprinkling?
Learn from this that the leftovers on the finger are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָּמַר הַזָּאָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling, and רבא's reading that supports it, that שירים שבאצבע are פסולין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Washing is needed only for fit blood. The ברייתא requires washing for blood that sprays before all the sprinklings are done, so leftover blood on the finger must be fit.

steps.title: The ברייתא means before or after each single sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבין בר רב אדא's reading. The ברייתא is talking about each single sprinkling, not about finishing all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If the blood sprayed before a sprinkling left his hand, the garment needs washing. If it sprayed after a sprinkling left his hand, from what was left on his finger, it does not need washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reading from the last step. It says 'after he sprinkled' means after each single sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין בר רב אדא read 'after' as 'after all the sprinklings,' which would make the leftover blood fit. The גמרא reads it as 'after this one sprinkling.' So the blood left on the finger is already unfit, and a garment it sprays onto does not need washing. That fits רבא and רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A sprinkling of blood
Washing (of a garment the blood fell on)
Sprayed, splashed
From what was left over (on the finger)

steps.confusionAlert: Only blood that is still fit to sprinkle makes a garment need washing. So 'no washing needed' here is a sign that the leftover blood is unfit.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָצְתָה מִיָּדוֹ הַזָּאָה –
phrases.english: No, before a sprinkling left his hand,
it requires washing,
but once a sprinkling has left his hand
and it sprayed from what remained,
it does not require washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָצְתָה מִיָּדוֹ הַזָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that leftover blood is fit
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'After he sprinkled' can mean after each single sprinkling, not after all of them.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the פרה אדומה משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the משנה that the כהן wipes his hand on the cow only after finishing the sprinklings. So before that, he does not wipe, which suggests the leftover blood is fine to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: When he finished sprinkling, he wipes his hand on the body of the cow. When he finished, yes. When he has not finished, no.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new challenge to רבא from the משנה about the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says he wipes his hand only after he finishes. אביי infers that between sprinklings he does not wipe at all. That means he keeps using the blood on his finger, so it must still be fit, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He finished sprinkling
Wipes off
The red heifer
Yes

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
When he finished sprinkling,
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in מסכת פרה, about sprinkling the red heifer's blood.

phrases.english: he wipes his hand on the body of the cow.
When he finished, yes;
when he did not finish, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא challenge is pushed aside, אביי brings a new challenge from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that leftover blood on the finger is פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he wipes only after finishing, he does not wipe between sprinklings, so the leftover blood must be fit.

steps.title: רבא: before finishing he wipes his finger
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that after finishing, the כהן wipes his whole hand. Before finishing, he still wipes his finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When he finished, he wipes his hand. When he has not finished, he wipes his finger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'no' in the משנה is about wiping the whole hand, not about wiping at all. Between sprinklings he wipes just his finger, which removes the unfit leftover blood. So רבא's view still works.

keyTerms.meaning: His hand
His finger

phrases.english: He said to him:
When he finished, he wipes his hand;
when he did not finish, he wipes his finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Before finishing, there is no wiping at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before finishing, he wipes his finger, just not his whole hand.

steps.title: Where would he wipe his finger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. Wiping the hand on the cow makes sense, but where would he wipe the finger? If on the cow, the משנה should have said so. Since it did not, the finger does not need wiping.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that after he finished, he wipes his hand on the cow's body, since it is written 'And the cow shall be burned in his sight.' But if before finishing he wipes his finger, what does he wipe it on? If you say on the cow's body, the משנה should have taught 'he wipes his hand and his finger on the cow's body.' Since it does not teach that, we learn that the finger does not need wiping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's answer. It asks where the finger would be wiped, and it concludes from the משנה's silence that no wiping is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hand is wiped on the cow because the blood is supposed to be burned together with the cow. If the finger were wiped on the cow too, the משנה would have listed 'hand and finger' together. Since it only mentions the hand, the leftover blood on the finger seems fine to use, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for this part, but...)
With what? On what?
It should have taught
Learn from this
Wiping

steps.whyThisMatters: This puts רבא's view that leftover blood is פסול under serious pressure again.

phrases.english: It makes sense that when he finished, he wipes his hand
on the body of the cow,
as it is written: “And the cow shall be burned in his sight,”
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:5. The פסוק goes on to list 'her blood,' so the blood is burned along with the cow.

phrases.english: but if when he did not finish he wipes his finger,
on what does he wipe it?
For if you say on the body of the cow,
it should have taught:

phrases.aramaic: מְקַנֵּחַ יָדוֹ וְאֶצְבָּעוֹ בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה!
phrases.english: He wipes his hand and his finger on the body of the cow!
Since it does not teach that,
learn from this that it does not need wiping.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא גָּמַר מְקַנֵּחַ יָדוֹ בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the finger is wiped between sprinklings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no good place to wipe the finger. If it were wiped on the cow, the משנה would have said 'hand and finger.' Its silence shows the finger is not wiped, so the leftover blood is fit.

steps.title: The finger is wiped on the edge of the bowl
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the כהן wipes his finger on the rim of the מזרק, and hints to this from the words כפורי זהב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He wipes his finger on the edge of the bowl, as it is written: "Bowls (כפורי) of gold."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had asked where the כהן could wipe his finger, since the משנה only mentions wiping on the cow. אביי answers: on the edge of the bowl holding the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This saves רבא's answer from step 25. The משנה did not need to mention finger-wiping because the finger is wiped on the bowl, not on the cow. The פסוק calls the bowls כפורי, which sounds like a word for wiping, so the bowl is the place for wiping.

keyTerms.meaning: The rim or edge of the bowl that holds the blood
A bowl used in the בית המקדש to hold the blood of a קרבן
"Bowls of gold" (עזרא 1:10). The word כפורי is linked to wiping.

steps.whatToRemember: Between sprinklings, the finger is still wiped, on the edge of the מזרק. Only after all the sprinklings is the whole hand wiped on the cow.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
On the edge of the bowl,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן wipes his finger on the rim of the bowl holding the blood.

phrases.english: as it is written: "Bowls of gold, etc."
phrases.notes: עזרא 1:10. The word כפורי sounds like the Aramaic word for wiping, so the bowls are a place for wiping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 about where the finger would be wiped, and so defends רבא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a location the משנה did not need to mention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה only mentions wiping on the cow, there seems to be nowhere to wipe the finger, so maybe it is not wiped at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finger is wiped on the edge of the מזרק, so there is no need for the משנה to mention it.

steps.title: Did רבי אלעזר really say that? The case of the חביתי כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי אלעזר's earlier ruling about blood split between two vessels, and challenges it from his view that the חביתי כהן גדול becomes holy in halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי אלעזר really say this? But it was stated about the חביתי כהן גדול: רבי יוחנן says it is not made holy in halves. רבי אלעזר says: since it is offered in halves, it is made holy in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier topic: רבי אלעזר's ruling that blood split between two vessels does not become holy. It now asks whether he really holds that, since elsewhere he says something that sounds opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתי כהן גדול is a מנחה brought half in the morning and half in the afternoon. רבי אלעזר says that because it is offered in halves, putting half in one vessel and half in another makes it holy. That seems to contradict his ruling that a full amount must go into one vessel to become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: "Did he really say this?" The opening of a challenge that sets one statement of a sage against another statement of his
The daily flour offering of the כהן גדול, fried on a griddle. Half is offered in the morning and half in the afternoon
Becomes holy in halves, meaning each half in its own vessel still becomes holy
"Since...". It gives the reason for the ruling that follows

steps.confusionAlert: This is a change of topic. The wiping discussion is finished. The גמרא is now going back to an earlier ruling of רבי אלעזר about blood in two vessels.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא now has to show how the two rulings of רבי אלעזר fit together. That answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Elazar really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" is his earlier ruling that blood split between two vessels does not become holy.

phrases.english: But it was stated:
The High Priest's griddle-cake offering:
Rabbi Yochanan says:
it is not made holy in halves,
Rabbi Elazar says:
since it is offered in halves,
phrases.notes: Half is offered in the morning and half in the afternoon.

phrases.english: it is made holy in halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומי אמר רבי אלעזר הכי והא איתמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wiping discussion and returns to רבי אלעזר's earlier ruling about blood split between two vessels.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that blood split between two vessels does not become holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר says the חביתי כהן גדול becomes holy in halves, which seems to contradict his ruling that a full amount must be placed in one vessel to become holy.
